newsitem.title: UK: Rubber forum to study future of tyre industry.
newsitem.headline: Rubber forum to study future of tyre industry.

text.p: A two-day International Rubber Forum that starts on Thursday will evaluate the changing structure of the tyre and non-tyre industry especially in Europe, the organisers said on Wednesday.
The International Rubber Study Group (IRSG) said the gathering, which coincides with the group's annual meeting, would also examine the outlook for world natural and synthetc rubber supply.
The forum comes at a time when natural rubber prices have fallen sharply to three-year lows after hitting a peak in 1995.
The benchmark RSS3 rubber prices on the Singapore futures market are hovering at 115 U.S. cents per kg, the lowest since June 1994 and compared with nearly $2.00 in April 1995.
Traders cited the seasonal production uptrend, good crop weather and flat consumer demand as the main contributory factors.

The IRSG forum will be attended by about 150 rubber traders and industry officials. The forum's spotlight will be on the world's tyre giants, who consume about 70 percent of natural rubber production.
Natural rubber's greatest competitor is synthetic rubber produced from oil and chemicals but both are used in tyre production.
The world's tyre sector is now dominated by five or six tyre manufacturers including U.S. firm Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co and French group Michelin.
"What's happening is that these firms are more acquisitive, buying up plants in Eastern Europe or beginning to look to joint ventures and acquisitions in China," one industry official said.
The London-based IRSG groups 23 countries that supply and use most of the world's natural and synthetic rubber.
